coreIdea: O=upper bound, Ω=lower bound, Θ=tight bound. Use limit-ratio test f(n)/g(n) as n→∞ to compare. Hierarchy: log < poly < exponential < factorial.
mustRememberFormulas: lim f/g = 0 → f=o(g); = const → f=Θ(g); = ∞ → f=ω(g)
log n = o(n^ε) for any ε>0
n^k = o(c^n) for any k, c>1
Comparison sorting lower bound = Ω(n log n)

commonTrapsQuickList: O and Ω are NOT symmetric (only Θ is)
f=O(g) ⟺ g=Ω(f) (this direction IS always true — don't confuse with the false 'g=O(f)' claim)
log's base doesn't matter for asymptotic comparison
Only W(n)≥A(n) is universally guaranteed — no other fixed ratio exists
highYieldPyqLessons: TRUE/FALSE claim verification (9/22) and ordering (7/22) together are ~73% of this topic — the limit-ratio test solves both.
n^(log n) vs (log n)^n type comparisons recur — always take logs of both sides first when exponents themselves contain n or log n.
